title: Charter
text: The GEOTEC Journal Club is a monthly, 60–70 minute session where members discuss one paper to foster critical reading, debate and presentation: judging its methods, assumptions, results and contribution, as well as its academic writing style.

title: Charter
text:
Purpose

What it is

A space to debate a paper’s methods, assumptions, validity and writing, and to practise arguing about them.

What it is not

A way to keep up to date with a specific field or subfield, although every paper has a clear link to GIScience. Members work on different topics, so selected papers will not always connect to each member’s research.

Why it matters

It develops transferable competences in the ResearchComp framework, mainly critical thinking, analytical thinking and evaluating research.

title: Charter
text:
Who takes part
Open to all GEOTEC members: PhD students, faculty and other research profiles. Everyone takes a turn as facilitator.

title: Charter
text:
Roles

Facilitator

Selects the paper using the shared selection criteria, announces it one week ahead, gives the context and summary, and guides the discussion.

Attendees

Read the paper before the session and bring one question or critique.

title: Charter
text:
Ground rules







Everyone reads the paper, not only the facilitator.
Critique the paper, not the people.
“I didn’t understand X” is a welcome contribution.
The shared guiding questions frame every discussion.

title: Charter
text:
Record and review

Each session is archived on the group’s Quarto website: paper, facilitator, date, slides and key takeaways (see minutes).
At the end of each semester (6 sessions), members hold a short retrospective and may propose changes to this charter.

title: Guiding questions
text: Everyone reads the paper, not only the facilitator. Use these questions while reading and bring at least one question or critique to the session; the facilitator uses them to moderate the critical discussion (see the charter).

title: Guiding questions
text:
Scientific contribution

What is the research question, and why does it matter?
What is the claimed contribution, and is it new relative to prior work?
Is the data appropriate? How was it collected and preprocessed?
Are the methods sound? What assumptions are hidden?
Do the results support the conclusions?
What is reproducible? Are code and data available?
What would we do differently, or how could we use this?

title: Guiding questions
text:
GIScience or spatial checks






For papers with spatial data or methods, you may also ask:




Scale and MAUP

Would results change with a different spatial unit or resolution?

Validation

Does it account for spatial autocorrelation (spatial vs. random cross-validation)?

CRS and resolution

Are coordinate reference system and resolution choices justified?

Generalisation

Would the findings transfer to other regions?

title: Guiding questions
text:
Writing style

Do the title and abstract state the contribution clearly?
Does the introduction motivate the problem and position it in the literature?
Can you follow the methods well enough to replicate them?
Do figures and tables carry the argument on their own?
Are limitations stated honestly?
What would you borrow from or avoid in this paper when writing your own?

title: Guiding questions
text:
Your preparation






TipBefore the session, note:




One strength of the paper
One weakness or open question
One thing you would apply to your own research or writing

title: Paper selection criteria
text: The facilitator picks one paper of at most 15 pages, guided by the two core criteria below, and announces it to all GEOTEC members at least one week before the session.

title: Paper selection criteria
text:
Core criteria
Every selected paper should meet both criteria:



Table 1: Core selection criteria









Criterion
What to look for




Relevance to the group
A clear link to GIScience; topic, method or data of interest to several GEOTEC members, not only the facilitator


Methodological interest
A method, design or validation approach worth dissecting, even outside members’ own topics












TipWhy these criteria?



Because the club trains critical reading rather than keeping up with a topic, a paper with rich methods or instructive writing is a better pick than one that is merely new or close to your own thesis.

title: Paper selection criteria
text:
Practical requirements

Maximum 15 pages (excluding references and appendices)
Accessible to all members: open access, or a PDF shared with everyone
Readable by non-specialists in the group with reasonable effort
Not already discussed in a previous session (check the archive)

title: Paper selection criteria
text:
Occasional picks

Classic or landmark papers that everyone should know
Recent preprints
Controversial papers, which often teach the most about critical reading and debate

title: Paper selection criteria
text:
Announcement
At least one week before the session, the facilitator sends the following to all members (Geoinfo mailing list):

Full reference and DOI or link to the PDF
One or two sentences on why this paper was chosen
A reminder to bring one question or critique, using the shared guiding questions, to the session
